definitions.explanation: Strong sexual desire or craving, often with a negative or moralistic connotation. Originally a Buddhist term referring to one of the worldly desires that lead to suffering.

examples.japanese: {色欲|しきよく}に{溺|おぼ}れる。
{色欲|しきよく}は{仏教|ぶっきょう}で{煩悩|ぼんのう}の{一|ひと}つとされている。
examples.english: Lust is considered one of the worldly desires in Buddhism.

examples.japanese: その{王|おう}は{色欲|しきよく}に{目|め}がくらみ、{国|くに}を{滅|ほろ}ぼしたと{伝|つた}えられている。
examples.english: It is said that the king was blinded by lust and brought his kingdom to ruin.

notes:
A literary and somewhat formal term rooted in Buddhist philosophy. {色|しき} here refers to physical/sensory phenomena (particularly related to the body and sexuality), and {欲|よく} means desire or craving. In Buddhism, {色欲|しきよく} is one of the {五欲|ごよく} (five desires) that bind humans to the cycle of suffering.

In modern Japanese, the word carries a strong negative or moralizing tone and appears most often in literary, religious, or historical contexts rather than casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {色欲|しきよく}に{溺|おぼ}れる: to drown in lust
- {色欲|しきよく}に{目|め}がくらむ: to be blinded by lust
- {色欲|しきよく}を{抑|おさ}える: to suppress lustful desires

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {性欲|せいよく}: sexual desire — neutral, clinical term without moral judgment
- {欲望|よくぼう}: desire, craving — broader, covering all types of desire
- {煩悩|ぼんのう}: worldly desires — Buddhist term for all earthly cravings
